properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 4 at 9:13PM EDT until September 5 at 12:15AM EDT by NWS Raleigh NC
properties.description:
FFWRAH

The National Weather Service in Raleigh has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Edgecombe County in central North Carolina...
Southwestern Halifax County in central North Carolina...
Northern Nash County in central North Carolina...

* Until 1215 AM EDT.

* At 913 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rocky Mount, Tarboro, Nashville, Dortches, Red Oak, Princeville,
Whitakers, Conetoe, Castalia, Speed, Leggett, Battleboro,
Kingsboro, Glenview and Aventon.

This includes the following frequently flooded locations...
Tanner Rd at Compass Creek, Ethridge Farm Rd near Fishing Creek,
Bethlehem Church Rd at Maple Swamp, Batts Chapel Rd & US Hwy 258,
Cutchin Farm Rd near Deep Creek, Low lying areas on Dickens Rd and
Low Ground Rd near Fishing Creek.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Panther Junction, Persimmon Gap, Big Bend National Park and Chisos
Basin.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 4 at 8:09PM CDT until September 6 at 10:36AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier affecting Jefferson,
Hardin, Jasper and Orange Counties.

Village Creek Near Kountze affecting Hardin County.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Jefferson and Hardin
Counties.

For the Neches River...including Town Bluff, Evadale, Neches River
Saltwater Barrier...Minor flooding is forecast.
For the Village Creek...including Kountze...Moderate flooding is
forecast.
For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Village Creek near Kountze.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 21.9 feet, At this level, water will be flowing over
the Highway 418 bridge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CDT Friday the stage was 21.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM CDT Friday was 22.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tomorrow evening and continue falling to 5.9 feet Wednesday
evening.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 21.8
feet on 02/12/1966.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 815 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 4 at 10:20PM EDT until September 4 at 10:30PM EDT by NWS Raleigh NC
properties.description:
The storm which prompted the warning has weakened below severe
limits, and no longer poses an immediate threat to life or property.
Therefore, the warning will be allowed to expire.  However, gusty
winds and heavy rain are still possible with this thunderstorm.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 4 at 8:27PM CDT until September 4 at 10:30PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 827 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is 1.5 to 2
inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas especially along US Hwy 90 of Northeastern
Brewster and far Southeastern Pecos Counties.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.
